new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-27 (City Council adopted signed Resolution No. 2932 at a special meeting, effective immediately)
new_candidates.duration: 120 days unless extended or repealed, with mandatory council review before expiration
new_candidates.legal_basis: Resolution No. 2932, adopted by the Hillsboro City Council at a special meeting on July 27, 2026
new_candidates.trigger: City sought time to study data center and battery storage impacts and develop code amendments; contemporaneous coverage described Hillsboro as the first Oregon city to adopt a data center land-use moratorium
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of the July 31, 2026 research date. Effective immediately upon adoption, the resolution bars submission, acceptance, processing, or approval of new land-use applications for new or expanded data centers or battery energy storage systems as primary uses. Applications already under review are not affected. Runs 120 days (to approximately 2026-11-24) absent extension or repeal, with council review required before expiration.
new_candidates.affected_projects: New or expanded stand-alone data center or battery energy storage system land-use applications submitted after July 27, 2026; does not affect applications already under review.
new_candidates.outcome: Enacted moratorium on new data center and battery storage land-use applications while the city studies impacts and develops code amendments.

evidence.title: Resolution No. 2932 (Amended, Signed)
evidence.supports: Full signed resolution text establishing a 120-day land-use moratorium on new or expanded data center and battery energy storage applications, effective immediately.

evidence.title: Hillsboro approves data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Reports adoption of the moratorium and describes it as the first Oregon city land-use moratorium of its kind.

new_candidates.notes: Distinct from the same council's Resolution No. 2931 (July 21, 2026), a 180-day pause on new Strategic Investment Program tax-abatement agreements for stand-alone data centers, which is excluded from this packet as a subsidy/tax-incentive eligibility freeze rather than a land-use moratorium. Also excluded on the same basis is Oregon HB 4084, a statewide enterprise-zone tax-incentive moratorium that took effect 2026-06-05.
